correctness.rationale: Conditional on assignment history, a newly protected position is globally top-choice with probability r_j/n, whereas an unprotected position avoids envying the t_j previously protected allocations with probability r_j/(r_j+t_j). Adjacent interchange of one protected status and one unprotected status leaves the product unchanged; hence the k-wise event equals the final-k-positions probability k!/n^k for every specified set. Summing joint events gives falling-factorial moments (n)_k/n^k, binomial inversion the exact distribution and pgf convergence 1/(2-z). Independently implemented profile enumeration over all 24^4=331776 n=4 strict preference profiles and exact subset probabilities for n<=9 corroborated the identity. No independence of the indicators is claimed.

value.rationale: Exact k-wise intersection probabilities give an unusual position-exchangeable statistic despite position-sensitive marginals, and the non-Poisson geometric limit yields a natural complete probabilistic law for simultaneous absence of both directions of envy.

final_claim: Under n-by-n independent uniform complete strict preferences and random serial dictatorship, for any k specified serial positions the probability each both receives her overall first choice and is envied by nobody equals k!/n^k; these intersection indicators are exchangeable and their count converges to geometric(1/2), with exact mean 1, variance 2(1-1/n) and displayed inclusion–exclusion distribution.
